Topps Baseball continued the trend of a small flagship set. Split between two series, it runs just 503 cards. 1998 Topps Series 1 has 282 cards while Series 2 has just 221. Cards have a fairly thick gold border, which is a big change from the white borders of recent years. The nameplate at the bottom of the card goes heavy on the foil with the player's name in large block letters. The foil at the bottom of the letters go on to form a block that holds the team name.
Topps Baseball has one parallel set, Minted in Cooperstown. Cards have a bronze foil plaque on the card fronts that were were stamped on-site at the National Baseball Hall of Fame.

Topps Baseball has lots of basic inserts that focus primarily on the game's biggest stars. Etch-a-Sketch is one of the more unique inclusions. The cards use artwork from George Viosich III, who used the Etch-a-Sketch toys as his canvas to draw detailed images of the nine featured players. Inserted in Series 1 packs, Inter-League Mystery Finest inserts use a cover to hide who's on the card. Collectors must peel the cover off to not only reveal the player, but whether it's a basic version or a Refractor. Series 2 Mystery Finest cards follow a similar approach but the player is displayed. The mystery element is to reveal which version of the card. Each of the 20 cards have Bordered, Borderless, Refractor and Borderless Refractor variations.
